# Comparing runs and risk

## Ensembles and sensitivity runs

`jbplot_ensemble()` compares a list of fits (scenarios, sensitivity runs, the
steps of a workflow), as JABBA's plot of the same name: trajectories coloured
by run and a Kobe plot with each run's terminal uncertainty and its median.
With `joint = TRUE` the runs are pooled with equal weights into one ensemble.

```{r cmp-runs}
fsch <- jabba3(d, jb3_priors(d, r = c(0.2, 0.5)), jb3_model(shape = "schaefer"), osa = FALSE)
runs <- list(Fox = fit, Schaefer = fsch, `Lag + AR(1)` = rec)
```

```{r cmp-ensemble, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
jbplot_ensemble(runs)
```

```{r cmp-ensemble-joint, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
jbplot_ensemble(runs, joint = TRUE)
```

`jbplot_summary()` gives the overview of JABBA's `jbplot_summary()`: B, F,
$B/B_{MSY}$, $F/F_{MSY}$ and $B/K$ by run, and the production curves with
$B_{MSY}$ and MSY.

```{r cmp-summary, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
jbplot_summary(runs)
```

### Sensitivity runs with `update()`

A fit stores its data, priors, model and settings, so `update()` refits it with
only the inputs that change. Priors and model options are changed by name, with
the arguments of `jb3_priors()` and `jb3_model()`; all other inputs and settings
(engine, draws, OSA, workflow) are taken from the fit. With `lapply()` a
sensitivity analysis takes one line per factor:

```{r cmp-update}
sens.r <- lapply(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.4), function(r)
  update(fit, priors = list(r = c(r, 0.5)), run = paste("r =", r)))
sens.sdb <- lapply(c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2), function(s)
  update(fit, priors = list(sdb = c(s, 0.3)), run = paste("sdb =", s)))
names(sens.r)   <- sapply(sens.r, `[[`, "run")
names(sens.sdb) <- sapply(sens.sdb, `[[`, "run")
t(sapply(c(sens.r, sens.sdb), function(f){
  s <- f$ts[f$ts$year == max(f$years) & f$ts$quantity %in% c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"), ]
  stats::setNames(round(s$est, 2), s$quantity) }))
```

```{r cmp-update-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
jbplot_ensemble(sens.r)
```

Some priors are derived from others when `jb3_priors()` is called: the FishLife
prior on the process-error SD (`sdb`) and the default `kdyn` from `r`, and the
default `K` from the catch. By default `update()` changes only the priors that
are named, so the `r` runs above keep the `sdb` prior of the base fit. Dependent
priors can be set explicitly (`priors = list(r = c(0.4, 0.5), sdb = c(0.15, 0.3))`),
or re-derived from the new values with `recompute = TRUE`:

```{r cmp-update-recompute}
fr <- update(fit, priors = list(r = c(0.4, 0.5)), recompute = TRUE)
rbind(base = fit$priors$sdb, `r = 0.4` = sens.r[[3]]$priors$sdb, `r = 0.4, recompute` = fr$priors$sdb)
```

The same works for model options, the workflow and the engine, e.g. a final NUTS
run of the selected configuration:

```{r cmp-update-other, eval = FALSE}
update(fit, model = list(lag = 3, rho = 0.75), run = "lag + AR(1)")   # model options
update(fit, workflow = "tier1", amat = 3)                             # rerun as a workflow
update(fit, engine = "nuts", nuts = list(iter = 2000))                # same inputs, NUTS
update(fit, data = d.new)                                             # new data, same settings
```

`kobe = FALSE` drops the Kobe panel in `jbplot_summary()` and `jbplot_ensemble()`.
`jabbaplot3()` takes a list of runs too, with a choice of panels:

```{r cmp-jabbaplot3, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6.5}
jabbaplot3(runs, panels = c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy", "Catch", "kobe", "production", "procdev"))
```

### Weighted ensemble

`jb3_ensemble()` combines the runs into one weighted ensemble, as the
GFCM/ICCAT JABBA ensembles: each run contributes a number of draws
proportional to its weight, and the joint draws give the ensemble
trajectories, reference points and status. `jb3_weights()` scores each run on
diagnostics (convergence, runs tests, RMSE, and optionally hindcast MASE and
Mohn's rho with `hindcast` and `retro`); `weight = "equal"` gives equal
weights:

```{r cmp-weights}
w <- jb3_weights(runs)
w
ens <- jb3_ensemble(runs, weights = w$weight)
ens
```

The ensemble behaves like a fit in the plots, tables and projections:

```{r cmp-ensemble-w, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
jbplot_ensemble(ens)
```

### Short-term advice with the HCR (GFCM)

`jb3_fwd()` and `jb3_hcr()` take the ensemble as they take a single fit
(chapter *Projections*): each member's own model (production function, lag,
AR(1) process error) is projected on its share of the draws, so the forecast
carries the structural uncertainty between the runs. As in the GFCM Type 1
management procedure: two intermediate years at the status quo catch, the
hockey-stick rule ($B_{trigger} = B_{thr} = 0.5 B_{MSY}$) applied to the
ensemble $B/B_{MSY}$ in the TAC year, and the fishing opportunities for
$F_{adv}$, $F_{tgt}$, $F_{sq}$, $C_{sq}$ and $F = 0$:

```{r cmp-ens-hcr}
y0  <- max(ens$years)
yrs <- y0 + 1:4
csq <- mean(tail(fit$data$catch, 3))
fsq <- mean(tail(ens$ts$est[ens$ts$quantity == "F/Fmsy"], 3))
ctrl <- function(v, q) data.frame(year = yrs, value = c(csq, csq, v, v), quant = c("Catch", "Catch", q, q))
hcr.ens <- jb3_hcr(jb3_fwd(ens, list(Ftgt = ctrl(1, "Fmsy"))), ftgt = 1, btrigger = 0.5, blim = 0.3)
hcr.ens
```

```{r cmp-ens-hcr-plot, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 6}
jbplot_hcr(hcr.ens)
```

```{r cmp-ens-stf, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 8}
fc.ens <- list(Fadv = ctrl(hcr.ens$Fadv, "Fmsy"), Ftgt = ctrl(1, "Fmsy"), Fsq = ctrl(fsq, "Fmsy"),
               Csq = ctrl(csq, "Catch"), F0 = ctrl(0, "Fmsy"))
stf.ens <- jb3_fwd(ens, fc.ens)
jbplot_projection(stf.ens)
```

The fishing opportunities table gives the catch and F in the TAC year $y$ and
the biomass response at the start of the following year $y+1$ (`osa = TRUE`,
the default): the biomass is the start-of-year biomass,
$B_{y+1} = B_y + P(B_y) - C_y$, so the effect of the TAC in $y$ appears in
$B_{y+1}$. The change in biomass is $B_{y+1}$ relative to $B_{y-1}$, the start
of the last intermediate year, as in `FLRef::fwd2type1()`:

```{r cmp-ens-table}
knitr::kable(jb3_fwdtable(stf.ens))
```

### Long-term TAC projections

For the medium- to long-term consequences of TAC levels, catch scenarios as
multiples of the current catch (`Csq`, mean of the last three years), with
three intermediate years at the current catch and a horizon of about two
generation times:

```{r cmp-prjens}
cr <- seq(0, 1.6, 0.2)
prjens <- jb3_project(ens, scenarios = setNames(lapply(cr, function(m) c(Csq = m)), paste0(100*cr, "% Csq")),
                      nyears = 31, imp.years = 3)
```

```{r cmp-prjens-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8}
jbplot_projection(prjens, type = c("B/Bmsy", "Catch"))
```

Catches above the surplus production deplete the stock in the long term; the
projected catch is capped at 95% of the biomass, so the catch falls once the
stock is depleted. The Kobe matrices take the ensemble projection in the same
way as a single fit, e.g. `jb3_kobematrix(prjens, what = "all", percent = TRUE)`.

## Risk curves

`jbplot_crisk()` plots, as JABBA's `jbplot_Crisk()`, the probability that
$B < B_{MSY}$, that $F > F_{MSY}$ and that $B < 0.5 B_{MSY}$ (`bfrac`) against
the scenario value (catch or F/F~MSY~), one line per projection year. It takes
any projection with several catch or F scenarios, of a single fit (e.g.
`jbplot_crisk(pj)` for the F/F~MSY~ scenarios of the chapter *Projections*) or
of an ensemble. The catch level at which a risk curve crosses a chosen
probability (e.g. 0.5, or a lower risk tolerance) in a given year is the
corresponding catch advice.

### U.S. advice: risk plots with MSST

Risk plots of this kind support U.S. advice (NOAA, SEDAR assessments), where the
biomass limit is the minimum stock size threshold, e.g.
$MSST = (1 - M) B_{MSY}$ as in the JABBA assessment of great hammerhead for
SEDAR 77 (SEDAR 2024). A named `bfrac` labels the panel, and `x = "ratio"`
shows the catch relative to the current catch, as `type = "ratio"` in JABBA's
`fw_jabba()`. For the ensemble projection:

```{r cmp-crisk-msst, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 9}
M <- 0.3                                          # natural mortality (illustrative)
jbplot_crisk(prjens, years = seq(2025, 2045, 5), bfrac = c(MSST = 1 - M), x = "ratio")
```

MSST can also be drawn on the projection plot, `jbplot_projection(prjens, bthr = c(MSST = 1 - M), blim = NULL)`.
